learningObjective: Identify examples of operator-level IRs used in production and the features that characterize them.
stem: Which of the following statements about operator-level (graph-level) IRs used in production ML compilers are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: XLA HLO / StableHLO and ONNX are operator-level IRs: computations are expressed as coarse-grained ops (matmul, convolution, softmax) with SSA values carrying shape and dtype annotations.
Graph-level passes over operator IRs commonly include shape inference, constant folding, algebraic simplification, layout choice, and operator fusion.
TVM Relax and PyTorch FX are examples of operator-level graph IRs used before lowering to tensor-expression or loop-level IRs.
Operator-level IRs typically expose loop iteration variables to graph-level passes, so tiling and vectorization are directly expressible at the operator IR level.

explanation: A, C, D are correct: HLO/StableHLO and ONNX are operator-level IRs with typed values; Relax and FX are also operator-level IRs used before tensor/loop-level lowering; and common graph-level passes include shape inference, algebraic simplification, layout choice, constant folding, and operator fusion. B is wrong: operator-level IRs do not expose loop iteration variables — that is precisely what distinguishes them from tensor-expression / loop-level IRs.

optionExplanations.D: Wrong: exposing loops is what loop-level IRs do; operator-level IRs treat iteration implicitly.

assumptions: The classification uses the standard three-layer IR view (operator/tensor/loop).
nonImplications: Does not imply operator-level and loop-level IRs cannot coexist in one compiler (MLIR is designed around exactly this coexistence).
Does not imply that operator-level IRs are strictly weaker; they compose well with lower-level layers.

distractorRationales.D: Blurs the distinction between operator-level and loop-level IRs.
